deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.label: AArch64 · ARMv8.2 SHA3 extension
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.registers.label: AArch64 · ARMv8.2 SHA3 · vector registers
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.covers.thetaRhoPi: Round {{round}} · θ ρ π: A[{{sx}},{{sy}}] → A[{{x}},{{y}}]
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.note.loadState: Loads lanes of the state A[25] from memory. Each lane goes into the low half of its own vector register (a d-register load clears the high half), so the 25 lanes occupy 25 registers for all 24 rounds.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.note.parityPartia: eor3 XORs three registers at once. The column parity C[x] = A[x,0] ⊕ … ⊕ A[x,4] takes two of them: this first one combines rows 0–2 (the trace's θ “partial” value).
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.note.parity: The second eor3 of the column adds rows 3 and 4 to the partial value: the register now holds the column parity C[x].
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.note.rax1: rax1 computes D[x] = C[x−1] ⊕ ROT(C[x+1], 1) in one instruction: rotate the second source left by one bit and XOR it with the first.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.note.xar: xar XORs a lane with D[x] (θ) and rotates the result right (ρ: a left rotation by the lane's offset is a right rotation by 64 minus it). π costs nothing: the compiler simply writes the result into the register of the lane's new position.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.note.xarNoRotatio: Lane A[0,0] has ρ offset 0, so this xar rotates by 0: it is only θ's XOR with D[0]. Its π position is (0,0) again.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.note.xarLate: clang scheduled this xar after the first χ instructions (they do not need its lane yet). Its value is still the lane after θ, ρ and π, but because spans never run backwards it is shown at the χ step, where it executes, not at θ … π.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.note.bcax: bcax (bit clear and XOR) computes a ⊕ (b ∧ ¬c), exactly χ: A[x,y] ⊕ (¬A[x+1,y] ∧ A[x+2,y]), one lane per instruction.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.note.loadRc: Loads the round constant RC for ι from a table (x9 = table address, x8 = 8 × round). The compiler places the load in the middle of χ, well before ι uses it, so it appears at the χ step.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.note.iota: ι: XOR the round constant into lane A[0,0]. This is the last instruction of the round.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.note.spill: Out of registers: 25 lanes plus C, D and temporaries do not fit into 32 vector registers, so the compiler spills lane A[1,4] to the stack …
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.note.reload: … and reloads it from the stack, into a different register, just before its xar needs it.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.note.calleeSave: Saves registers d8–d15 of the caller (the AArch64 calling convention requires preserving them). Their values come from outside the hash and are not shown.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.note.calleeRestor: Restores the caller's registers d8–d15 before returning. Their values are not part of the trace.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.note.loop: Back to the start of the loop until all 24 rounds are done. At this point each lane is in the same register as at the loop's start, so the next round finds it there.
deriver.isa-armv8-sha3.note.zip1: zip1 puts the low halves of two registers side by side: two lanes in one q register, so that a single stp stores four lanes.
